resources.string: Port state, host mode and attached devices
No USB state from the framework
No USB power supply in sysfs
Type-C state only in the charger driver
USB drive attached but not mounted
The sticky USB_STATE broadcast was never sent: UsbDeviceManager found no gadget driver (neither /sys/class/android_usb nor configfs), so MTP and ADB over USB cannot work.

init did not apply the requested USB configuration: sys.usb.state stays behind sys.usb.config. A function is missing from init.usb.rc / configfs (for example the f_ffs instance for adb or mtp), or the UDC name in sys.usb.controller is wrong.

The data lines are connected but the host never selected a configuration: the PC has no driver for the composition, or a gadget function failed to bind. Try another function (MTP vs. charging only) and check dmesg for the UDC.
The charger driver detects a PC or hub port, but the gadget side reports no connection: the UDC is not bound, VBUS is not passed to the controller, or the Type-C mux does not route D+/D- to it.
Connect the phone to a PC to test MTP and ADB over USB.
No usb, pc_port or ac entry in /sys/class/power_supply (or SELinux hides it): charger detection cannot be checked.
Plug in a charger or a PC to check detection, input current and voltage.
The battery service says a charger is plugged in, but no USB power supply is online in sysfs: the health HAL reads a different supply than the one checked here.

Power supply %1$s is online but the battery service says nothing is plugged in: healthd/health HAL does not read that supply, so charging is not shown and charging-related behaviour (screen on, alarms) is wrong.
The charger is detected with a 0 mA input limit: charger type detection (APSD) or AICL in the charger driver failed, so the phone may not charge. The battery area shows the current flowing.
VBUS reads %1$s V, outside the range of a USB source: the charger driver reports a wrong unit or a bad ADC channel.

No standard Type-C class: roles are handled privately by the PHY, charger or a vendor Type-C driver (common on older kernels). The framework then shows no USB port in Settings, but OTG can still work.

The kernel has a USB host controller but FEATURE_USB_HOST is not declared: android.hardware.usb.host.xml is missing, so UsbManager ignores attached devices. Kernel drivers (storage, keyboards) still work.
FEATURE_USB_HOST is not declared and no host controller is active. If the phone supports OTG, add android.hardware.usb.host.xml.
On dual-role controllers (dwc3) the host side appears only while an OTG adapter or device is attached. Attach one and run again.

The kernel enumerated devices but UsbManager lists none: UsbHostManager filters them (config_usbHostDenylist) or cannot open /dev/bus/usb (ueventd permissions, SELinux). Apps cannot talk to these devices.
The kernel enumerated devices; apps do not see them because FEATURE_USB_HOST is not declared.
Attach a flash drive, keyboard or hub with an OTG adapter to test host mode.
The volume is in an error state: unsupported filesystem (exFAT or NTFS without kernel or FUSE support) or a damaged drive. Try a FAT32 drive.

A mass-storage interface is enumerated but no removable volume is mounted: vold ignored the disk. Check the voldmanaged entry for the USB host path in fstab, the filesystem support and SELinux denials for vold.
Attach a USB flash drive with an OTG adapter to test mounting.
A HID interface is enumerated but no external input device exists: the kernel HID driver (CONFIG_USB_HID, hid-generic) is missing, or /dev/input permissions block InputReader.
Attach a keyboard or mouse with an OTG adapter to test input.
Data role, gadget functions and power input, live
No USB device attached. Use an OTG adapter or a USB-C hub.
A USB drive is attached but not mounted yet.
Is the flash drive mounted, with its files visible in the Files app?
Type here with the USB keyboard
Do the keyboard keys type and does the mouse pointer move and click?
Plug the phone into a wall charger, then into a PC: the port card above should show the charger type and the current limit change.
Is charging from a wall charger and from a PC detected, with the charging indicator on?

To act as a host the phone must switch the controller to host role and power the bus. On micro-USB this is triggered by the ID pin of the OTG adapter (grounded); on USB-C by the Rd resistor of the adapter, seen by the Type-C controller. The phone must then output 5 V on VBUS (boost regulator, \"otg\" supply in the charger driver). If nothing enumerates, check in dmesg that the role switch happens and that VBUS is enabled; a powered hub helps to tell power problems from data problems.
